claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi is a single-phase FCC alloy with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
Previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
Approximately 10–15 at.% Mn should be substituted for Fe, Co, Ni, or a combination of those elements.
The proposed Mn substitution preserves a near-equiatomic, high-entropy composition.
The proposed composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Arc melting, homogenization, and low-temperature annealing will maintain the single-phase FCC structure.
Mn incorporation will induce localized lattice distortions.
Mn incorporation will induce subtle chemical ordering.
Mn-induced local strain and mild antiferromagnetic interactions will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy will enhance domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
A 10–15 at.% antiferromagnetic-element substitution can increase coercivity in a high-entropy alloy.
The Mn-substituted alloy will have statistically significantly greater coercivity than baseline FeCoNi.
High saturation magnetization will be retained after Mn substitution.
The Mn-substituted alloy will remain single-phase FCC.
The coercivity improvement applies only when Mn remains at approximately 10–15 at.% and processing prevents phase separation or secondary phases.
The exact coercivity increase is uncertain because it depends on Mn distribution, local ordering, and processing.
Identically processed baseline and Mn-substituted samples can be compared using XRD, TEM or APT, and room-temperature hysteresis measurements.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies only 10–15 at.% Mn in a four-element alloy, whereas the predicted outcome says the resulting alloy remains overall equiatomic. A genuinely equiatomic quaternary alloy would contain about 25 at.% of each element; the exact Fe/Co/Ni fractions are also left unspecified.
